easy.def: To move from one place to another.
examples: I go to school by bus.
We went to the park.
The train goes fast.

more.def: To move or travel from one place to another, or to leave a place.
examples: Every summer we go to the lake for a week.
The ducks went down the stream in a line.
She has gone to the library to return her books.

easy.def: Something you want to do and work hard for.
examples: My goal is to read ten books.
I kicked the ball to score a goal.
His goal is to learn to swim.

more.def: Something you are trying to reach or achieve.
examples: Her goal is to learn to play the violin this year.
Our class goal is to collect five hundred cans of food.
He set a goal to save enough money for a bike.

easy.def: A farm animal with horns that likes to climb.
examples: The goat ate grass.
The goat has a beard.
A goat climbed the hill.

more.def: A farm animal with horns and a short tail that is raised for milk, meat or wool.
examples: The goat climbed to the top of the rock.
We got milk from the goat.
A baby goat is called a kid.

easy.def: A female god in stories and religions.
examples: The goddess lived on a mountain.
A goddess is a female god.
The goddess had magic powers.

more.def: A female god, as in the myths of ancient Greece and Rome.
examples: In the myth, the goddess lived on a mountain.
The Greeks prayed to a goddess of the harvest.
The goddess of the sea calmed the waves.

easy.def: A shiny yellow metal.
examples: The ring is gold.
Pirates look for gold.
The crown is made of gold.

more.def: A shiny yellow metal that is valuable and used to make jewelry.
examples: The crown was made of solid gold.
Miners once searched the river for gold.
She wears a gold ring.

easy.def: Shiny and yellow, like the metal.
examples: A gold star.
Gold stickers.
Her dress was gold.

more.def: Having the shiny yellow color of the precious metal.
examples: She won a gold medal.
The gold sunset lit the lake.
He glued gold stars to the card.

easy.def: Shiny yellow, like gold.
examples: The golden sun shone.
She has golden hair.
The prize was a golden cup.

more.def: Shiny yellow like gold, or made of gold.
examples: The golden wheat swayed in the breeze.
The queen wore a golden crown.
The leaves turned golden in the fall.

easy.def: A game where you hit a small ball into holes with a club.
examples: Grandpa plays golf.
Golf is played outside.
We played mini golf.

more.def: A game in which players use clubs to hit a small ball into a series of holes.
examples: Grandpa plays golf on Saturday mornings.
The golf course has wide green grass.
In golf, the player with the fewest hits wins.

easy.def: A word that shows surprise.
examples: Golly, that is big!
Golly, look at that!
Oh golly!

more.def: An old-fashioned word that people say when they are surprised.
examples: Golly, that is a big fish!
Oh golly, I forgot my hat!
Golly, what a nice surprise!

easy.def: Nice, and just right.
examples: This is a good book.
She is a good friend.
The soup smells good.

more.def: Of a high quality, pleasant, or helpful.
examples: Sunshine and rain are good for the garden.
He is a good swimmer and has won many races.
It is a good idea to wear a helmet.

easy.def: Kind and doing what is right.
examples: He is a good boy.
She was good to the new girl.
Be good for the sitter.

more.def: Behaving well, and showing kindness or honesty.
examples: The good neighbor shoveled snow from our walk.
Our puppy was very good at the vet's office.
It was a good thing to return the lost wallet.

easy.def: A word you say when you leave.
examples: Goodbye, Grandma!
We said goodbye at the door.
Wave goodbye.

more.def: Something you say when you or another person is leaving.
examples: She waved and called goodbye from the bus window.
We said goodbye to our friends at the end of camp.
Goodbye, everyone; see you tomorrow!

easy.def: Being good.
examples: I believe in goodness.
Her goodness shines.
The goodness of a kind heart.

more.def: The quality of being good or kind.
examples: We admired her goodness.
The goodness of the people made the town warm.
His goodness showed when he helped the lost child.

easy.def: A word you say to show surprise.
examples: My goodness!
Goodness me!
Thank goodness!

more.def: A word used to show surprise or relief.
examples: My goodness, what a big dog!
Thank goodness you are safe!
Goodness, it is late.

easy.def: A word you say at bedtime.
examples: Goodnight, Mom.
I said goodnight.
Goodnight, sleep tight.

more.def: A word you say to someone before going to sleep.
examples: Goodnight, Mom, I love you.
I said goodnight and turned off the light.
"Goodnight, sleep tight," said Dad.

easy.def: Things that are made to be sold.
examples: The store sells goods.
The truck carries goods.
The ship brought goods.

more.def: Things that people make, buy and sell.
examples: The shop sells goods from around the world.
Trucks carry goods from the factory to stores.
The ship delivered goods to the port.

easy.def: Kind feelings and a wish to help.
examples: She showed goodwill.
A smile shows goodwill.
Goodwill makes friends.

more.def: A friendly, kind feeling toward others.
examples: She showed goodwill to the new student.
The gift was a sign of goodwill.
Goodwill makes it easier to make friends.

easy.def: A treat to eat.
examples: Mom brought goodies.
I ate a goody.
The bag was full of goodies.

more.def: A tasty treat, or something nice.
examples: Mom brought goodies to the party.
The bag was full of cookies and other goodies.
We shared the goodies after the game.

easy.def: To make a silly mistake.
examples: I goofed on my spelling.
She goofed up the game.
He goofed and dropped it.

more.def: To make a silly mistake, or to play around and act silly.
examples: I goofed on the last spelling word.
We goofed around at recess and laughed a lot.
He goofed and put salt in the cake instead of sugar.

easy.def: A silly mistake.
examples: That was a goof.
I made a goof.
The goof was funny.

more.def: A silly mistake, or a person who acts silly.
examples: That was a silly goof on my part.
My brother is such a goof that he makes everyone laugh.
She made a goof and put on two different socks.

easy.def: Silly.
examples: The clown is goofy.
I made a goofy face.
The goofy dog tripped.

more.def: Silly and playful in a funny way.
examples: I made a goofy face in the mirror.
The goofy puppy chased its tail.
He wore a goofy hat to the party.

easy.def: A big bird with a long neck that swims.
examples: The goose honked.
A goose swam in the pond.
Geese fly south.

more.def: A large water bird with a long neck and webbed feet.
examples: The goose honked and flapped its wings.
A flock of geese flew south in a V.
The goose swam across the pond.

easy.def: Very, very pretty.
examples: The sunset was gorgeous.
She has a gorgeous smile.
The garden looks gorgeous.

more.def: Very beautiful, so lovely that you stop and look.
examples: The sky was a gorgeous pink at sunset.
She wore a gorgeous gown to the ball.
The mountains looked gorgeous after the first snow.

easy.def: A very big, strong ape.
examples: The gorilla sat in the zoo.
A gorilla is big.
The gorilla ate a banana.

more.def: The largest kind of ape, with a strong body and black fur, that lives in Africa.
examples: The gorilla beat its chest in the zoo.
A gorilla can weigh over three hundred pounds.
The baby gorilla clung to its mother.

easy.def: A word you say when you are surprised.
examples: Gosh, it's big!
Gosh, what a day!
Oh gosh!

more.def: A word used to show surprise.
examples: "Gosh, that is a huge cake!" said Mia.
Gosh, I forgot my homework.
"Oh gosh," he said, "it's already noon."

easy.def: A kind of religious music.
examples: The choir sang gospel.
I like gospel music.
We heard a gospel song.

more.def: A style of religious music with strong singing and a lively beat.
examples: The choir sang gospel in church.
I like gospel music because it is joyful.
We heard a gospel song at the festival.

easy.def: Talk about other people that may not be true.
examples: Do not spread gossip.
The gossip hurt her.
I do not like gossip.

more.def: Talk about other people's private lives, which is often unkind or untrue.
examples: Do not listen to gossip about your friends.
The gossip about the new girl was not true.
Gossip can hurt people's feelings.

easy.def: The people who lead a country or state.
examples: The government makes laws.
The mayor works for the government.
There is a new government.

more.def: The group of people who rule a country, state or town and make its laws.
examples: The government built a new highway.
Our town's government plans the parks.
Leaders in the government met to talk.

easy.def: The leader of a state.
examples: Our governor visited the school.
The governor gave a speech.
She wants to be governor.

more.def: A person who is elected to lead the government of a state.
examples: The governor signed a new law for our state.
Each state in the country has its own governor.
The governor spoke at the opening of the new park.

easy.def: A long, fancy dress.
examples: She wore a gown.
The gown is blue.
The princess wore a gown.

more.def: A long, formal dress, or a loose robe worn for a special event.
examples: She wore a long gown to the ball.
The graduates wore caps and gowns.
The queen's gown sparkled.
